findings.title: Subdivision candidate counts are wrong, so the "multiplicative" claim is unsupported
findings.description:
The slice says S=3 alone drops candidates to ~5000, and to ~555 with early exit. Those are per-cell figures, not scan totals.

- **Actual scan total at S=3:** a 7×7 scan is 49 cells × ~555 ≈ 27,000 candidates. `148-notes.rediagnosis.md` (Intervention 2) states the same figure.
- **Actual gain from subdivision alone:** scanned area goes from 9r² to (7/3)²r² ≈ 5.4r², about 1.65×. The limit as S grows is 2.25×, not 9×.
- **With early exit:** the scan stops after roughly `max_neighbors` ÷ acceptance-rate tests regardless of cell size, so subdivision's marginal effect on capped agents is small and unquantified.

Intervention 2 carries most of the slice's new surface (config field, kernel parameter, CLI flag, validation). The plan assigns it here, so it stays. Correct the figures, and state what S is expected to buy: uncapped or sparse agents and a better acceptance rate. That way the A2/A3 gates are not read as depending on a 9× candidate reduction, and the architecture's "profile before you optimize" principle is met by a prediction that can be checked.

findings.title: Break sits outside the seam, so "A7 seam preserved" is overstated
findings.description:
Option A puts the termination test (`k_found >= max_neighbors and max_neighbors > 0`) in the kernel loop while `get_neighbors_first_k` keeps its own cap gate. That creates two problems:

- **Duplication:** the cap rule, including the "0 means uncapped" sentinel, now lives in two places.
- **Swap no longer local:** slice 145 defines the seam as the point where distance-ranked selection can replace first-k "without changing the tick kernel structure". Distance-ranked selection must keep scanning after k candidates are held, so the hard-coded break would have to be removed from the kernel at swap time. Line 112's claim that the swap point "remains intact" does not hold as written.

A light fix is enough: put the stop predicate in a sibling function beside the seam (for example a `scan_complete(k_found, k_max)` func) that the loop consults for the break. Selection and termination policy then change together.

findings.title: Step 3 ablation cannot distinguish its four cases
findings.description:
The four runs are two pairs of identical commands: "baseline, counter-gating" and "early exit only" are the same S=1 invocation, and likewise the two S=3 runs. Intervention 1 replaces counter-gating and defines no toggle, so the counter-gated runs cannot be produced from the slice's own build.

Cut the ablation to what the plan's exit criteria need:

- Take the baseline from the recorded slice 145 measurement (or a run on the pre-slice commit).
- Run S=1 and S=3 on the new build.

Keeping the S=1 run matters. S=1 is the default that slice 146 inherits, while headroom is only gated at S=3 (line 128). Do not add an early-exit toggle just to serve the ablation.

The commands also use `python scripts/bench.py --config … --N … --parity-check numpy`. The slice 145 and 148 walkthroughs invoke `uv run python -m migratory.bench.cli --backend … --workload …`. Align them, or name the new flags as scope.

findings.title: A5 spill check names tooling the CUDA host does not have
findings.description:
A5 is to be confirmed "via `nvcc --ptxas-info` or benchmark log". Step 4 (line 182) relies on "`TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS=1` or equivalent". `148-notes.envelope-measurement.md` §2A records that `ptxas`, `cuobjdump` and `nvcc` are not installed on that host. The baseline "local memory = 0" was established there by counting `.local` declarations in the hot kernel's PTX from the Quadrants kernel cache.

As written, the gate has no runnable procedure and the environment variable is a guess. Specify the same PTX `.local` inspection used for the baseline, so the before and after figures are comparable.

findings.title: Break exits only the candidate loop; the cell loops keep running
findings.description: After the cap fires, the `drow`/`dcol` loops still visit every remaining cell. That is up to 48 more cell headers at S=3 and 288 at S=8, each computing a cell index and reading its bounds before breaking again. Finer subdivision therefore raises post-cap overhead. Repeating the cap check at the cell-loop level makes "exits after ~32" true.

findings.title: Rationale for the S ≤ 8 bound does not hold
findings.description:
The scan covers the same physical radius at any S, so it cannot be "larger than the physical neighborhood". Cell-count arrays at S=8 are also tiny: about 121×121 cells for the 756-unit world against a 24 GB card. Either drop the upper bound or justify it by scan-cell count, and define it once as a named constant instead of the inline literal.

Separately, line 53 uses `query_radius` where slice 145 defines cell size from `max_query_radius`. State which applies for multi-profile workloads.

findings.title: Warp-coherence premise is not established by the referenced design
findings.description:
The divergence argument assumes threads in a warp are spatially adjacent agents. Slice 145 iterates agents by index `i` and keeps spatial order only in the `sorted_agent_ids` indirection. Warp-mates are therefore not necessarily neighbours.

The conclusion still stands: a warp runs only as long as its slowest thread, which is far short of 45,000 iterations unless it contains an uncapped agent. The stated reason should be corrected.

findings.title: How slice 146 obtains S is not stated
findings.description: S is described as a `BenchConfig` field and `setup()` is declared unchanged. The slice does not say how a non-bench caller supplies S. Add one sentence: either S is a backend setup input, or 146 owns the choice. This keeps "Slice 146 is unblocked" accurate.
